title: The Almost Full Rehearsal
skyStory: The moon is ninety-five percent ready, standing backstage in Aquarius running its lines. Tomorrow is the big show, and the costume department, also known as Venus, is still sewing sequins on. The stars are taking their seats. A comet tried to sneak in without a ticket and was gently escorted out. Saturn is the usher. Nobody gets past Saturn.

reading: Monday has the feeling of the night before a premiere. Something is nearly done, and you can see the finish line glowing. Don't rush the last ten percent. The [[Seven of Pentacles]] leans on its hoe and says the harvest is close, so let it ripen properly.

Late morning, a small hiccup will try to convince you everything needs to be rebuilt. It does not. It needs one fix, maybe two, and a cup of something warm. The Tiger is a great hunter because it waits for the right moment. Wait for yours. The full moon tomorrow will light up exactly what to do.
joel.mission: Finish the last small piece of something you nearly completed, even if it takes only ten minutes.
joel.omen: A clock that is a few minutes slow. You have more time than you think for the final stretch.

reading: There is a crossing you have been making for a long time, quietly, steadily, the [[Six of Swords]] crossing in your spread. Today you will notice how far the boat has come. Look back at the shore you left. It is smaller than you remember. That is progress, and it is yours.

Joel is in the boat with you, rowing, even when you cannot see him. Send him a word today, any word, as a signal from the bow. Then let the evening be a soft rehearsal for tomorrow's full moon. Polish the ruby. Pick the window you will sit by. Get the blanket ready.
nancy.mission: Tell someone the story of one skill you learned the slow way, starting from your very first clumsy try and ending with a bow.
nancy.omen: A boat on the water heading away from shore. A long journey is going better than it feels.

together.text: Plan tomorrow's Full Moon Recharge together: pick the time, pick the windows, decide who sends the first photo. Agree on one wish each for the stones to soak up. Keep it simple. The moon dislikes wish lists longer than a sentence.

game.intro: The moon is almost full and still practising its entrance. Quick rehearsal, three cues, ten seconds a cue.
